"""Skyline-to-terrain matching: where could a camera stand to see this horizon?

The outline of hills against the sky is a fingerprint of the place it was seen
from. This module

1. traces the skyline in a picture (where sky meets land, column by column),
2. loads free elevation data around a candidate place (AWS Terrain Tiles,
   "terrarium" PNGs: SRTM/ASTER/national lidar, ~10-30 m in most of the world),
3. renders the horizon a person standing at each point of a search grid would
   see, all the way round, allowing for the curvature of the earth, and
4. slides the traced skyline along every rendered horizon, at several plausible
   lens widths, and keeps the position and compass heading that fit best.

It is a measurement, not a model: no AI is involved, and the residual (how many
degrees the two outlines differ) is reported as is. It only works where the
skyline is land against sky with real relief (hills, crags, mountains); trees,
buildings and flat horizons are refused rather than matched.

content.text:
I've finished looking through the code. These suggestions are ranked by what matters most for the demo and for the live site at earwitness.ussr.pl.

## 1. Security on the live site (fix before judging)
- **`POST /api/cases/from-path` can read any file on the server.** Any logged-in user can pass a path like `/srv/earwitness/.env`. The server copies that file in as "evidence", and `GET /api/cases/{id}/files/...` then serves it back. That would leak the OpenAI, Gemini and database keys (`src/earwitness/server/app.py:159`). Either remove this endpoint on prod, or only allow paths under one directory you choose, and only for an admin account.
- **Any logged-in user can delete or rerun anyone's case.** Each case already stores `uploaded_by`, so check it, with an admin override.
- **Nothing limits uploads or concurrent cases.** There's no size cap, and `EARWITNESS_PARALLEL` only limits modules inside one case. A few large uploads at once could exhaust the box during the demo. Add a size cap, a global case queue, and a simple rate limit per user.
- If Auth0 sign-ups are open, "logged in" means anyone. Consider an allowlist of judges and teammates.

## 2. Reliability work
- **Run the evaluation automatically.** `scripts/evaluate.py` on the real clips and the HEIC/WhatsApp photo set is your most valuable check, but it only runs when someone remembers. Store the expected verdicts in a file and add a single command (or a pre-deploy step in `deploy.sh`) that fails if any real original is flagged as edited.
- **Make the geo ground truth an automatic check.** The Würzburg lane, the Borders moor and Holyrood are currently only in notes. Turn them into a geo regression with distance-error thresholds, so changes to `terrain.py` and `georefs.py` can be measured.
- **Add CI.** There's no `.github/workflows`. Running ruff, `tsc -b` and the tests that don't need the database (`test_auth`, `test_terrain`, the photo suite) on every push would catch most breakage.
- **Test titles against the verdict rules.** The verdict depends on findings' title prefixes ("Taken on ", "ENF dates"…), so renaming a title can silently change the answer. Move those to tags or constants, or add a test that each prefix `brief.py` matches is still produced by some module.

## 3. Code structure
- **`brief.py` is 1,580 lines and `photo_provenance.py` is 1,300.** Splitting `brief.py` into video rules, photo rules and the AI narrative would make the verdict logic easier to check. That's the part judges will ask about.
- **`terrain.py`, `georefs.py` and `tests/test_terrain.py` are uncommitted** even though `geo.py` already uses them. Commit them, or a fresh deploy from git will break geo.
- **The `kana` language label has no entry in `web/src/lib/plain.ts`.** That was the only gap my script found. It's minor, but Japanese transcripts may show a raw label.
- The mock or preview layer (`mock*.ts`, `MockPreviewBar`) ships in the production bundle. Put it behind `import.meta.env.DEV` or a build flag.

## 4. Features for "discover the invisible"
- **Show a confidence breakdown for each verdict:** which tagged findings pushed it to EDITED or POSSIBLY, and which signals were checked and came back clean. Non-expert judges trust a verdict more when they can see the evidence for and against.
- **Add a "what we couldn't check" list for each case**, such as no audio (so no ENF), no GPS, or a flat skyline (so terrain matching was refused). This fits your rule of stating limits.
- **Offer side-by-side comparison of two cases** (an original against a WhatsApp copy, or two clips of the same event). Re-encoding traces and metadata differences become obvious.
- **Add a signed, exportable report:** the existing HTML report plus SHA-256 hashes, module versions and a timestamp, so the chain-of-custody story is complete.
- **Show the terrain match visually:** the rendered horizon overlaid on the photo's skyline, with the residual in degrees. It's a striking "invisible made visible" moment and needs no AI.

## 5. Demo polish
- Pre-run the demo pack on prod and pin those cases, so the judges' walkthrough doesn't wait on live AI calls or Overpass.
- Make it easy to compare AI providers on the same case (OpenAI, Gemini, or your own Gemma on Ollama). Showing "Gemma, self-hosted" with comparable results is a good point for G-Research.

class Case:
    def __init__(
        self, case_id: str, workdir: str, filename: str, options: dict[str, Any]
    ):
        self.id = case_id
        self.workdir = workdir
        self.filename = filename
        self.options = options
        self.created = time.time()
        self.events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.listeners: set[asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]]] = set()
        self.status = "queued"
        self.ctx: CaseContext | None = None
        self.task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        self._log = None

    @property
    def evidence_path(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(
            self.workdir, "evidence" + os.path.splitext(self.filename)[1].lower()
        )

    def emit(self, event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        event = {"seq": len(self.events), "ts": round(time.time(), 3), **event}
        self.events.append(event)

        if self._log is None:
            self._log = open(os.path.join(self.workdir, "events.jsonl"), "a")

        self._log.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
        self._log.flush()

        for queue in list(self.listeners):
            queue.put_nowait(event)

    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        case_event = next((e for e in self.events if e["type"] == "case"), None)
        findings = [e["finding"] for e in self.events if e["type"] == "finding"]
        brief = next(

                e["artifact"]["data"]

Yes: cases that were partway through analysis when the server restarts now finish on their own when it comes back up. The new restart test and the auth, AI and database suites pass. It isn't committed or deployed yet.

**What happens after a restart**
- **Cases partway through analysis** are put back in the queue and run again, one at a time. Running them one by one means a restart with several unfinished cases doesn't overload the server.
- **They start over rather than picking up where they stopped.** The checks pass results to each other in memory, so a case can't safely resume halfway. AI answers are cached in each case's folder, so the rerun doesn't pay for them again.
- **The case explains it:** the rerun's log says the server restarted during the analysis and it was run again from the start. Anyone watching gets a refresh, the same as a manual rerun.
- **Deleting a case, or rerunning it by hand, while it waits its turn** is fine: the resume skips it. A case that fails doesn't stop the rest.

**Uploads cut off mid-transfer can't be recovered**, because the sender's browser has gone. Uploads are now saved under a temporary name and only renamed once complete. After a restart, a case whose file never finished is deleted instead of being analysed as a broken file. This can't detect partial uploads from before this change, since they were saved under the final name.

The manual "Rerun" button now uses the same reset code. The changes are in `src/earwitness/server/jobs.py` and `app.py`, with the test at the end of `tests/test_modules.py` and the behaviour described in `docs/PROTOCOL.md`.

**Why it was refreshing:** the photo's EXIF stores its 72 dpi resolution as a PIL fraction type that JSON can't encode. The photo-provenance check put that value in its data. The server then kept the event in memory even though saving it had failed. Every page load and WebSocket connection for the case crashed on it, so the page kept reconnecting.

**The fix (`dea3f96`):** the code that cleans event data before it's sent (`_jsonable`) now converts any kind of number to a plain one, and anything else to text. The server also encodes each event before keeping it, so one bad value can't break a case's page again. I reran the same photo locally: no bad events, no errors. A new test covers it, and the photo suite passes.

**A deploy problem it uncovered (`d864f52`):** one deploy stopped halfway with "Text file busy". The ffmpeg version check in `remote_setup.sh` always failed, so every deploy re-downloaded ffmpeg and copied it over the binary a running case was using. The check is fixed, and installs now copy the file aside and then rename it. The last deploy finished cleanly without touching ffmpeg.
